slides.title:
Monitor an airline service agent
and build better evaluations
slides.body:
Investigate booking mistakes, test a monitoring rule, and turn reviewed incidents into checks for the next version.
Six hours · Basic Python · Simulated airline data · Your own Forge project
Technical preview: native Alignment judging and prepared Insights remain unqualified.
slides.notes: Set the situation before introducing products. Participants operate a simulated airline customer-service agent. They will distinguish a request completing, a booking being correct, and a monitor detecting a problem. Those are three separate observations.
slides.name: introduction

MIT license · source checksums and assignments ship with the teaching data · this workshop adapts the environment rather than replicating its benchmark score

slides.title: Record a conversation around the passenger’s request
slides.body: <AirlineMechanism mode="spans" :reveal="$clicks + 1" />
slides.notes:
A conversation may contain several turns. Do not collapse unrelated requests into a single conversation. The passenger’s clarification and confirmation belong with the relevant turn evidence. Use native session and span identities from execution.

Visual sequence: Read the parent tree alongside operation order. Both model calls and both tool attempts remain children of their turn. Bar width is schematic, not measured latency. Ask participants which event needs the error and which needs the returned reservation; then map them to my_model_span and my_tool_span.
slides.name: trace-shape

slides.title: The tracing code records the actual tool result
slides.body:
```python {1-3|4-5|6-8|all} with tracing.Tool( name=record["name"], arguments=record["arguments"], result=record["result"], tool_call_id=record["id"], started_at=stamp(record["started_at"]), ended_at=stamp(record["ended_at"]), ) as span: if record.get("error"): span.record_error(RuntimeError(record["error"])) ```

Excerpt from my_tool_span. Arguments, results, timing, and errors come from the saved operation.
slides.notes: Name the actual function to edit. The SDK uses the recorded timestamps, not the time an export retry happens. Preserve the saved event if trace publication fails; retry only the export.
slides.name: tool-tracing

slides.title: Connect each model request to its response
slides.body:
In my_model_spanRecorded sourceWhat to inspect
model / response_modelRequested and returned model IDsWas the intended model used?
input_messages / output_messagesActual request and replyWhat did the agent know?
started_at / ended_atRequest timestampsWhere was time spent?
usageProvider-reported token countsWhat usage was actually available?

Missing usage remains missing. An exporter must not convert an unavailable token count into zero.
slides.notes: Open the editable my_model_span function beside this table. Participants supply these actual fields to tracing.LLM. Tool spans and model spans answer different questions; neither replaces the independent booking check.

slides.title: Define a behavior that a reviewer can check
slides.body:
Unrequested itinerary change
The agent changed or removed a flight outside the passenger’s approved change.

Judge the requested scope, the action, and the resulting reservation together. A shorter itinerary alone is not enough.
slides.notes: The initial proposed criterion is intentionally a starting hypothesis for alignment, not a validated native rule. Participants must review what evidence exists in each turn. Requests may authorize replacing the entire itinerary.
slides.name: tag-definition

slides.title: Fewer flights can be the correct result
slides.body: <AirlineMechanism mode="nonstop" :reveal="$clicks + 1" />
slides.notes:
This is the central counterexample to a naive flight-count rule. Ask the room whether changing three segments to two is sufficient evidence of failure. It is not.

Visual sequence: The connecting point disappears while the origin, destination, and return remain. Ask whether fewer segments is a failure before revealing the approved nonstop. The answer depends on the request, not the count. These segment names and airport positions are illustrative.
slides.name: counterexample-nonstop

slides.title: Add counterexamples before trusting the rule
slides.body:
ExampleWhat the criterion must account for
A one-way bookingThere was never a return flight to preserve.
An explicitly approved full-itinerary changeAll original flights may legitimately be replaced.
A failed write followed by successful recoveryJudge the resolved state and the turn’s scope.
A request waiting for confirmationNo write has been approved yet.
Missing original bookingInsufficient evidence is not a negative finding.
slides.notes: Human review comes before this optional calibration pack. Create six controlled calibration traces only after saving a booking review. Use actual reviewed turns when available. The calibration pack is a labeled teaching fallback, not a claim about the learner’s live failure rate. Keep all disagreements and their reasons.
slides.name: counterexamples

slides.body: <AirlineMechanism mode="criteria" :reveal="$clicks + 1" />

Walk through native Tags and Alignment. Creating or editing a notebook rubric is not the same action as saving native tag criteria. Use the native identities in the readback record.

Visual sequence: Keep the right-hand saved criterion in place while the Alignment draft is tested. Only the final explicit-save arrow changes live criteria. A failed Alignment test produces no judgment; it does not silently disable, update, or validate the saved live rule.

slides.notes: This is a local structured-response exercise for the explanation judge, separate from the native tag’s server-side implementation. A string false is not a boolean false. Preserve unavailable judgments rather than replace them with false.

slides.title: Measure the monitor on reviewed cases
slides.body: <AirlineMechanism mode="confusion" :reveal="$clicks + 1" />
slides.notes:
Walk through one cell at a time. The human review is the reference for this calculation; disagreement remains open to correction. Unavailable judgments are excluded from these eight processed rows and reported separately.

Visual sequence: Reveal the true positives, false positive, and remaining cells in place. Human review supplies the reference labels. These eight rows are illustrative arithmetic and not a successful native Alignment result. No unavailable prediction enters this matrix.
slides.name: confusion

slides.title: Precision asks whether an alert deserves review
slides.body: <AirlineMechanism mode="precision" :reveal="$clicks + 1" />
slides.notes:
The denominator is the tagged turns with a reviewed label, not all requests. Alert count cannot tell us how many failures were missed. Ask which example produced the false positive.

Visual sequence: The outlined row is the denominator: all four reviewed alerts. Three are reviewed failures. The faded second row is irrelevant to precision but needed for recall. If there are no alerts, leave precision unavailable. This graphic does not describe native workshop outcomes.
slides.name: precision

slides.title: Recall asks which failures the monitor missed
slides.body: <AirlineMechanism mode="recall" :reveal="$clicks + 1" />
slides.notes:
Precision and recall happen to match in this arithmetic example, but they use different denominators. Show the missed failure cell. Review sampling affects whether these values estimate the wider traffic population.

Visual sequence: The outlined column is the denominator: all four reviewed failures. One was not alerted. The same 75 percent hides a different question from precision. Review unflagged controls so this missed-failure cell can be populated. The arithmetic remains illustrative.
slides.name: recall

slides.title: Coverage tells us which turns were judged
slides.body: <AirlineMechanism mode="coverage" :reveal="$clicks + 1" />
slides.notes:
A missing tag is not enough to identify a completed negative judgment. Read processing status and identities. Keep pending, failed, insufficient-context, and scored states separate as supported by the recorded events.

Visual sequence: Count the eight completed predictions, then divide by all ten eligible turns. Only after that do we join completed predictions to human reviews for the agreement matrix. The two question marks remain unknown. Positive live assignments by themselves cannot establish this denominator.
slides.name: coverage

Keep the live assignment view separate from the explicit Alignment-test result set. Do not infer processing coverage from positive assignments alone. Record the denominator and native result source beside any calculated rate.

slides.title: Score the change and the preserved flights separately
slides.body:
Requested segment rangeCorrect replacement
Untouched segmentsStill present
Passenger approvalBefore the write
Airline policyApplicable rules met
slides.notes: The state scorer is deterministic over recorded state. It does not use the agent’s final assertion as proof. A completion score must fail when the requested change is missing, even if the unchanged return is preserved.
slides.name: state-scoring

slides.title: The explanation judge answers a different question
slides.body:
Booking-state check

Was the approved itinerary applied without changing unrelated flights?

Explanation judgment

Did the final response accurately describe the recorded work and unresolved issues?

“Your return flight is unchanged” can be wrong even when it is polite and well formatted.

Local fixture

Agent behavior

The agent still has to select the right flights, ask for approval, and report the result.

The worked repair establishes a mechanism. The matched evaluations establish how the tested agent behaved.
